time_scale_model: UTC→TAI applies hifitime's built-in leap-second table (27 s as of 2017, the table's last entry; pre-1972 UTC drift modeled). TAI→TT adds the fixed 32.184 s offset. TT→TDB adds the periodic relativistic term (amplitude ≈ 1.6 ms). Classical ΔT = TT−UT1 is not consumed by the ephemeris lookup: SPK segments are functions of TDB only, and ΔT belongs to Earth-rotation quantities computed by later layers.

files.name: chiron.bsp
files.source: JPL Horizons API SPK generation for 2060 Chiron (COMMAND='2060;', EPHEM_TYPE=SPK, START_TIME='1900-01-01', STOP_TIME='2050-01-02') at https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api; Horizons regenerates the file on request, so re-fetching may yield a different digest for the same solution. Re-fetched 2026-10-30 with the stop extended one day (2050-01-02) so coverage includes the fixture grid's final noon epoch, JD 2469808.0 = 2050-01-01 12:00 TT, which the previous 2050-01-01 stop fell 12 hours short of; byte size unchanged (2791424), digest refreshed, and solution equivalence re-verified by the unchanged Horizons reference fixture table in tests/fixtures.rs. Fetched again later the same day (2026-10-30) for the line-engine layer: Horizons regenerated the file with a new digest (same byte count, same parameters), digest refreshed and solution equivalence re-verified the same way
